prompt: How do I share my calendar in Outlook?
completion:
Below is a “cheat‑sheet” that covers the most common ways to share an Outlook calendar—whether you’re on the Windows desktop client, the Mac client, the web (Outlook.com or Office 365), or even the Outlook mobile app. Feel free to skip the steps that don’t apply to your setup. --- ## 1️⃣ Share from the Outlook Desktop Client (Windows) | Step | Action | Notes | |------|--------|-------| | 1 | Open **Outlook** → click the **Calendar** icon (bottom‑left). | | | 2 | In the navigation pane, locate the calendar you want to share (usually **My Calendar**). | If you have multiple calendars, choose the one you want. | | 3 | **Right‑click** the calendar and select **Share** → **Calendar…**
**or** click the **Share Calendar** button on the Home tab of the ribbon. | | | 4 | In the **Calendar Properties** window that opens, click **Permissions**. | | | 5 | Click **Add…** to enter the email address of the person (or Office 365 group) you want to share with. | | | 6 | Choose a permission level:
• *Can view when I'm busy*
• *Can view titles and locations*
• *Can view all details*
• *Can edit*
• *Delegate* | *Delegate* gives full control (create, edit, delete). | | 7 | (Optional) Click **Apply** → **OK**. | | | 8 | Click **Send** in the invitation window that pops up. | The recipient gets an email with a link to add your calendar to their Outlook. | **Revoking or Changing Access** - Right‑click the calendar → **Properties** → **Permissions**. - Select the user → **Remove** or change the permission level. - Click **Apply** / **OK**. --- ## 2️⃣ Share from the Outlook Desktop Client (Mac) | Step | Action | Notes | |------|--------|-------| | 1 | Open **Outlook** → click **Calendar**. | | | 2 | In the calendar list, right‑click the calendar → **Share** → **Calendar…** | | | 3 | In the dialog that appears, click **Add Person**. | | | 4 | Enter the email address and choose a permission level (same options as Windows). | | | 5 | Click **Send**. | | **Changing permissions** – Right‑click the calendar → **Calendar Permissions…**, edit or remove users. --- ## 3️⃣ Share from Outlook on the Web (OWA – Office 365 or Outlook.com) | Step | Action | Notes | |------|--------|-------| | 1 | Log into **Outlook.com** or your Office 365 webmail → click the **Calendar** icon (sidebar). | | | 2 | In the left pane, hover over the calendar you want → click the three dots (…) → **Sharing permissions**. | | | 3 | Click **Add people**. | | | 4 | Enter the user’s email address (or a Microsoft 365 group). | | | 5 | Pick a permission level:
• *Can view* (busy, free, details)
• *Can edit* | | | 6 | Click **Share**. | | | 7 | An invitation email is sent automatically. | | **Alternative: Share a link** - After selecting the calendar, click **Share** (at the top). - Choose **Get a link** → select *Can view* or *Can edit*. - Copy the link and send it manually. *(Note: link sharing is only available in the new Outlook on the web.)* **Revoking or adjusting** – Go back to **Sharing permissions**, click the **x** or **Edit** icon next to a user. --- ## 4️⃣ Share from the Outlook Mobile App > The mobile app has limited sharing features compared to desktop/web. > You can **view** shared calendars, but **granting** permissions is usually done via the desktop or web app. 1. Open the **Outlook** app → tap the **Calendar** icon. 2. Tap the **Menu** (☰) → **Settings** → **Calendar**. 3. Under **Shared calendars**, you can see calendars the app already has access to. 4. To add a new shared calendar, tap **+** → **Add a shared calendar** → **Enter email address** → **Add**. (This will prompt the desktop/web side to share if it hasn't already.) --- ## 5️⃣ Common Permission Levels (What Each Means) | Level | What the recipient can see / do | |-------|---------------------------------| | **Can view when I’m busy** | Only sees free/busy blocks. | | **Can view titles and locations** | Sees appointment titles, locations, and free/busy. | | **Can view all details** | Full event details, but cannot edit. | | **Can edit** | Can create, modify, and delete events. | | **Delegate** | Full control (acts like a second account). | --- ## 6️⃣ Tips & Gotchas | Tip | Why it matters | |-----|----------------| | **Always double‑check the email address** | A typo means no one gets the invite. | | **Use Office 365 groups** | One share to a group gives access to all members instantly. | | **Clear “No Access” first** | If you’re changing permissions, it’s safer to remove the user then add them back with the new level. | | **Accept the invitation** | The recipient must click **Add Calendar** in the email to see it. | | **Check your mailbox’s “Calendar Permissions” page** | For a quick audit of all shares. | | **Mobile restrictions** | If you can’t share from the app, switch to web/desktop. | --- ### Quick Recap 1. **Windows desktop** → Right‑click calendar → **Share** → add people → send. 2. **Mac desktop** → Right‑click → **Share** → add people → send. 3. **Web (OWA)** → Calendar → … → **Sharing permissions** → add people or get link. 4. **Mobile** → View only; do sharing from desktop/web. That’s it! Once the invite is accepted, your calendar will appear in the recipient’s Outlook, and they’ll see whatever level of detail you allowed. Happy scheduling!
